summary: Gone L-4 ground-house lookout in Sanders County, MT; built 1931 per listings, abandoned in the 1940s, collapsed under heavy snow in 1971.

facts.design: L-4 ground house with gable roof on a rock foundation
facts.status_note: Collapsed under heavy snow in 1971; register dates the collapse to winter 1971-72
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest (Noxon Ranger District)

events.note: July 2, 1930 Sanders County Independent-Ledger item: a new lookout station was being established, with a telephone line planned from Bull River Ranger Station.
Listed as built 1931 (firetower.org Built field; firelookout.com). Conflicts with the 1930 newspaper item.
Decade only: one of nine regularly staffed lookouts on the Noxon Ranger District in the 1930s.
Collapsed under heavy snow. Register says winter 1971-1972; other pages say 1971.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Listings give 1931; the July 1930 newspaper item describes a station being established. The story reports both and does not reconcile them.
Register says collapse in the winter of 1971-72; firelookout.com and the newspaper-based page say 1971. The story gives 1971 and notes the register's winter date.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict: listings say 1931, a July 1930 newspaper item (quoted on montanalookouts) describes the station being established. Collapse year: 1971 vs winter 1971-72. No source found on what remains at the site, or on access; the story says so and nothing more. One websearch.py lookup done; no NRHP or Forest Service page found. The firetower.org page mentions a Gary Weber photo with no usable URL, so no photo was added.
